newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish crown recovers vs mark, debt yields firm.
newsitem.headline: Swedish crown recovers vs mark, debt yields firm.

text.p: Swedish long debt firmed alongside the U.S. market in the early session on Tuesday and yields remained lower at midday.
The crown continued to strengthen against the dollar and recovered somewhat against the mark.
The market was mainly focusing on the U.S.'s second quarter employment cost index due out at 1230 GMT, dealers said.
"Today is a day of corrections. The trend of buying crowns at around 4.32 against the mark still holds, even if it's not as obvious today as the British pound continues to drop," one dealer said.
A dealer said the crown had not managed to break through the key 4.3250 resistence level so was still in a downward phase.
The crown firmed to 7.9187 against the dollar compared to 7.9523 late on Monday. The mark was changing hands at 4.3140 compared to 4.3055, off the day's lows of 4.3250.
Ten year bond yields dropped two basis points to 6.43 percent. Six month T-bill rate was two lower at 4.29 percent.
The central bank set its weekly repurchase operation at an unchanged, fixed rate of 4.10 percent as expected. -- Barbara Taltavull, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019
